articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks' (Digest No.134)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks

articleTitle: Integrated protection and auto-reclose control of source circuit breakers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Since the beginning of the electricity supply industry, power system protection have been designing and specifying protection and control schemes using a 'building block' approach, whereby discrete relays, more often than not from more than one manufacturer, are assembled and wired together to produce a complete control panel. Because of its inherent advantages, future protection relays of all types will utilise the 'integrated protection' technique. The author examines the integrated protection and auto-reclose control of source circuit breakers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of overhead electric lines for improved security
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The author describes the background and some aspects of the new design approach which was developed in anticipation of the 1988 Electricity Supply Regulations and used in the preparation of ESI Standard 43-40 'High Voltage Single Circuit Overhead Lines on Wood Poles'. The author demonstrates that to design for improved security at reasonable cost requires careful reconsideration of every aspect of the design process even involving reappraisal of the concepts of the design process itself.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improving supply security on 11-kV overhead network. The development of interconnected operation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The development of more intelligent relay equipment is being actively pursued. This, coupled with automated sectionalising and reclosing facilities, will permit normal interconnection of circuits with the ability to disconnect faulty sections and operate sound sections in a radial mode temporarily. Distance measuring protection relays, which have traditionally been applied to 132 kV and above networks, are becoming a reality at 33 kV and before long possibly at 11 kV. This would ensure clearance of faults within the accepted criteria for high speed protection, generally within 200 ms and certainly within 500 ms. Voltage restrain overcurrent relays which effectively grade on voltage as well as current are being examined. The author describes the development of such state of the art power network protection systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improvement in rural network performance (power system security)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Following the October 1987 hurricane in the UK, a reappraisal of engineering policies indicated that the only significant weakness was in Engineering Recommendation P 2/5 on security of supply, which did not address the problem of small groups of customers who regularly experience several supply interruptions each year. In order to tackle the problem of small Working Party was set up in South Eastern Electricity Board to identify those HV circuits with the worst fault record and suggest remedial measures for as many of them as possible. The results of this work are described by the author and form the basis for a programme starting 1988/89.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The electronic automatic sectionaliser link (power system protection)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The author describes electronic automatic sectionaliser links (sometimes known as ERICs) which have now become well established as a means of protection for overhead power line networks. There are probably around 1000-1500 such units currently installed on overhead lines, in locations as diverse as the North of Scotland, the Midlands and the South West of England. Their operating principles are given and performance results analysed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of cost benefit techniques on the design of rural networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Cost benefit analysis has played an important part in the design of Eastern Electricity's rural networks since the early 1970s. Initial applications were rule of thumb approaches (the familiar kVA km methods), however with the wider availability of computer facilities a number of the techniques have been refined to enable designs to be tailored for local network needs. The reliability techniques devised for this purpose are briefly described. They represent piecemeal application of cost benefit analysis. The author also describes current work in Eastern Electricity to unify these successful applications into a comprehensive rural network design computer program. The benefits of the proposal in the industry's new business environment are highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault handling techniques used by the ESB on 10 kV networks in rural Ireland
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The rural ESB 10 kV overhead network is operated with its neutral isolated from ground and consists of more than 18000 km of three phase, three wire backbone lines which feed a network of more than 54000 km of two phase, two wire lines. The author examines fault handling techniques used on 10 kV networks under three headings, earth faults, transient short circuits, and nontransient short circuits. The operation of the ESB's isolated neutral 10 kV system is commented on briefly for completeness.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic detection and indication of supply state on remote sections of overhead lines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: In common with many other supply authorities, Northern Ireland Electricity has no method of determining remotely whether supply is off or on beyond automatic sectionalising devices on rural overhead line networks. To improve service to the consumer some method of providing this information at the distribution control centres was considered desirable, possibly by utilising the public telephone network. Following discussion with British Telecom (Northern Ireland) a possible system is proposed which meets the requirements. These were that the system should be automatic, not affect the consumers telephone service or generate call charges, and have some form of alarm management at the control centre.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The co-ordination of protection and auto-reclose on 11 kV distribution networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The authors describe the co-ordination between the main line auto-reclosing circuit breaker and the fuse protection of a spur of an 11 kV distribution network. The relay has an instantaneous overcurrent set at 300 A, an instantaneous earth fault set at 120 A and an overall fault clearance time of 0.1 seconds.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hurricane force (power overhead lines)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The hurricane which hit the south east of England on the 16th October 1987 had a devastating effect on electricity supplies. It was apparent that previous refurbishment programmes had been ineffective in preventing damage, in particular the tree timing programme. The author looks at how future programmes may work in order to prevent so much damage.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Monitoring protection and switchgear performance on distribution systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Security of supply on 11 kV overhead line networks depends on many factors from the mechanical strength of the supports and conductors to the speed and discrimination of the protection and switchgear. Protection and switchgear must be considered together since it is their combined behaviour which determines how much of the network is disconnected when a fault occurs. Assessment of the performance of protection and switchgear, especially following the maloperation of one or the other, is difficult without quantitative data on the amplitude and duration of fault currents. The author presents a recorder which can monitor a number of circuits using a CMOS microprocessor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developments in microprocessor controlled sectionalisers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: In the past, overhead lines have been protected by the use of fuses. However fuses, being open to the elements, need regular maintenance and, when a fuse has operated, a field visit for replacement. A further disadvantage of fuses is that they cannot detect low levels of earth fault current. The authors describe how the versatility of the microprocessor controlled relay has been exploited to modify its operation from that of a recloser control relay to that of a sectionaliser control relay. The relay has the following features: remote operation, including remote closure for switches equipped with a closing coil; earth fault capability; and dead line detection down to 10% of setting.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remote automatic signalling system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The Northern Ireland Electricity (NIE) rural 11 kV distribution system is controlled by switchgear with automatic tripping and reclosing facilities operated by protection relays. This equipment is located either at 33/11 kV substations as circuit breakers or on overhead lines as ACR's and sectionalisers. In Craigavon area a network of 500 km of 11 kV overhead line is fed from 40 substations with 200 OCB's, 50 ACR's and 100 sectionalisers. On the NIE system, when a permanent fault occurs and automatic equipment opens or fuses blow, they rely completely on phone calls made by customers off supply, and subsequent analysis of these calls to ascertain the extent of the fault before assigning an engineer. During storm conditions this analysis can be very difficult and often there are delays because of the very large number of calls requiring sorting. After trying various methods the authors produce a system based on a telephone-linked burglar alarm system-the Scantronic Digital Communicator linked to various relays to analyse the performance of the various switchgear.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rural distribution system automation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The authors review current practice with the application of automatic sectionalising systems on distribution networks and consider recent developments in new pole top equipment to facilitate the extension of these systems. Some specification refinements are also considered. They describe three technically feasible methods of achieving automation of overhead high voltage distribution circuits. They detail a trial scheme encompassing all three operating modes where the hardware and automation philosophies will be tested and further developed. They also briefly consider some of the economic implications and application of automation to the distribution system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investment for improved supply security
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: In a period when high interest charges and high labour costs coincide, investments dedicated to a sole objective of widespread improvements of security on an initially sound 11 kV overhead power system are often difficult to support. The authors report on the long term measures initiated as part of a distribution asset replacement programme by the South of Scotland Electricity Board and the opportunities presented by this investment to achieve improved supply security.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Early warning pollution monitor for overhead line insulators to secure power supply
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The dominant fault in overhead power line systems is the flashover of insulators irrespective of voltage level. The authors examine the result of nearly ten years of extensive research and development work into an online insulator pollution monitoring system. Such a technique is described which depends upon the repetition of leakage current bursts to a certain set triggering value. The authors present the foreseen applications and advantages of this technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Non-damage fuse operations on 11kV overhead lines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Most 11 kV overhead line fuses are connected to spurs beyond a ground mounted circuit-breaker or, beyond a pole mounted circuit-breaker that is being operated as a source circuit-breaker. Group fusing, as above, has replaced the use of fuses in series and, largely, the fusing of individual transformers. However, even with group-fusing and the wide implementation of auto-reclosing, most fuse operations are still nondamage. The task for the fuse is that it should operate when the circuit-breaker recloses if a fault remains on the spur. Simple as this seems, it requires the circuit-breaker to operate before the fuse for the first protection operation, but the fuse to operate before the circuit-breaker for the second. The difficulty of placing the fuse characteristic between the instantaneous and delayed characteristics of the circuit-breaker is discussed by the author.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rural protection policy for long overhead networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The distribution of electricity to rural areas of Northern Ireland is by means of wood pole overhead lines energised at 11000 volts. The lines are supplied from three phase 33/11 kV transformers which have star connected 11 kV windings with the neutral star point solidly earthed. Many people live in isolated homesteads on the land that they farm and this makes low voltage distribution impracticable. 11 kV overhead lines are taken to individual homes and farms each of which has a pole mounted single phase transformer usually rated 5 kVA or 15 kVA. The authors describe Northern Ireland Electricity's power system protection policy for rural overhead networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Network 21C-an update (overhead system protection)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Three distinct stages of overhead power system operation have evolved in East Midland Electricity. Experience has shown that the majority of faults affecting the overhead system were transient, nondamage, and that the best performance, in terms of the lowest 'customer-hours lost' was achieved with minimum numbers of strategically positioned fuses, coupled with automatic reclosing 11 kV switches. This replaced the initial, heavily fused, system design. The third, and current, stage is still that of a minimum 'fused' system but with optimum use of source and pole mounted automatic reclosers, new electronic sectionalisers (which can replace fuses), fault passage indicators and automatic pole mounted isolators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An integrated actuator design for pole-mounted airbreak isolator (power system security)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The generally agreed desirability of remote control of 11 kV overhead network, so as to be able, in conjunction with other measures, to improve supply security, would be frustrated without an actuator with some form of energy store to operate the ubiquitous pole mounted airbreak isolator. The authors describe the design of an integrated actuator to carry out such operations. This actuator contributes to the security of supply on the networks by allowing isolation of faulty sections, and reinstatement of sound ones, in comparatively short times, direct from the control room.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability of rural distribution systems in developing countries
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The authors highlight some difficulties which influence the reliability of overhead primary distribution networks in developing countries. The performance characteristics and reliability of distribution systems in developing countries are constrained by the following factors: limited convertible (hard) currency; a scarcity of experienced and trained personnel in the power engineering sector; climatic conditions; lower energy usage per consumer and a larger proportion of the total load in rural areas; high growth rates; and poor communications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Operation of an isolated neutral 10 kV system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The Electricity Supply Board, Ireland, (ESB) 10 kV distribution system is in the main operated as an isolated neutral system, except in Dublin, where the 10 kV network has a resistance earthed neutral. The Dublin network is a cabled network. The author deals with the operational practices and procedures used in the operation of the isolated neutral 10 kV system and with the further development of these procedures in latter years. The major part of the 10 kV network is overhead, comprising about 72000 km of single phase and three phase lines, and about 3400 km of underground cables, mainly in towns and cities. The 10 kV LV transformers number 135000, of which approximately 120000 are single phase rural polemounted transformers, of 5 kVA, 15 kVA and 33 kVA ratings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Use of fault recorders to provide information during overhead line fault location and supply restoration procedures
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Northern Ireland Electricity are investigating various methods of optimising the application of telecontrol. The objective is for the control centre staff and field staff to work as a team with the control centre staff being able to co-ordinate the activities of the field staff more effectively because of the information available. A further objective is to minimise the need for field staff to visit the 33/11 kV substations during fault location procedures. The author outlines possible benefits of having data available, captured by fault recorders when the fault occurs. The argument developed in the paper is that clear fault information available to the control centre staff, in a readily understood format would enable the team to be more responsive to the fault condition, enhancing customer service to all affected by the fault.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault current indication and remote operation of overhead line switch disconnectors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Fault current indicators (FCIs) have been used successfully in South Wales on overhead power lines. Two ranges of FCI are used, one is permanently fixed to the overhead line support and the other, which is portable, is fitted during the course of fault investigation and removed when the fault position is found. The author discusses FCIs used in South Wales and how they are operated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Further developments in distribution switchgear for overhead networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Continuous development has been taking place in switchgear for overhead distribution networks. The author presents an update of the position of developments at the moment and discusses auto reclosers, sectionalisers and system automation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A low cost surveillance and remote control system for improving the performance of 11 kV overhead networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: 2.7 million customers in the UK are supplied from 11 kV overhead networks. On average, they lose their supply for about 4 hours each year compared with about 30 minutes for their counterparts in urban areas fed from underground cables. The reducing costs and increasing reliability of microprocessors have enabled Electricity Boards to install large telecontrol systems for the remote control of their primary distribution networks operating at 33 kV and 132 kV. This investment has enabled the Boards to minimise the effects of faults on the EHV network, but has not markedly reduced the duration of outages arising from the vulnerability of the extensive 11 kV networks, where most of the interruptions to customer supplies occur.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The co-ordination of reclosers, fuses and protection gaps
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Prior to 1984 the 11 kV overhead system in the North Yorkshire District of NEEB has suffered significant disruption during abnormal weather conditions and in particular lightning. As a first stage in attempting an improvement to the system its fault performance was studied in detail and one network in particular was singled out for remedial action. The network selected was fed from Sheriff Hutton Substation and was picked on the basis of its fault history of 219 incidents and 46000 consumer hours lost over a two year period, 162 incidents being due to non damage fuse operations. The application of the new fusing and triggered gap policy on the Sheriff Hutton system produced a considerable improvement in the lightning performance with, so far, no noticeable reduction in the performance during other abnormal weather conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
